rules.statement: A Family Court Judge has the power to issue a warrant of arrest in maintenance proceedings without initially issuing summons, provided they record their reasons in writing.
rules.supporting_quote: "There remains for consideration the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the failure of the learned Judge to record his reasons in writing before the issue of the warrant 141 renders it invalid. No doubt it is necessary that the Court must specify its reasons for the issue of a warrant of arrest against any person as required by law. But in my view this will only amount to an irregularity in the exercise of a power which is vested in Court. It is not a jurisdictional defect which would vitiate the subsequent proceedings in Court."
rules.statute_citation_verbatim: Section 15 of the Maintenance Ordinance (read with section 16 (1) of the Interpretation Ordinance), the provisions of section 63 (1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 applies to these proceedings.
